title: An in-body networking system for communication between wearable and implantable therapeutics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no text-mined accessions, only a subscription-required DOI link); Crossref metadata (Science 393:1322-1328, 17 authors, no licence, no related dataset DOI); Zenodo API searched for 'adz5300' (0 hits); Dryad API searched for 'adz5300' (0 hits) and 'in-body networking' (no matching record); Figshare API searched for 'adz5300' (no matching record); the publisher page returned HTTP 403. No data file of any kind was obtainable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the system itself comes from the abstract and press coverage only: the devices use tissue as a conductive medium, implants are syringe-injectable, coverage is claimed as >10x that of Bluetooth, and rat experiments demonstrated dual-limb motor control. No full text, no methods, no data availability statement, and no supplementary file list could be retrieved.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. Paywalled (publisher page HTTP 403), not in PubMed Central, Europe PMC reports no supplementary files and no data links, and searches of Zenodo, Dryad and Figshare on the DOI and title returned nothing. There is no dataset to download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL (not reached, but noted). No table exists. Any ML target here - for example received signal amplitude or whether a given implant switches on - would have to be built from figure traces in a supplement nobody can retrieve.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable: no files. Candidate inputs (transmit voltage, pulse width, electrode separation, tissue compartment) exist only as figure axes described in the abstract.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable: no data file or column list was retrievable.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on scale even if the supplement were open. This is a device-engineering paper with in vivo rat experiments; such papers report tens of devices and a handful of animals, far under the ~1,500 labelled rows the checklist requires. No count verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: well under 1 MB if any figure source data existed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here; there is simply nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable: no download to compare against the paper, and no full text to read the paper's own counts.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. Signals are physical electrical measurements rather than another model's output, so circularity is unlikely, but no provenance could be checked without the methods section.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: no data from this paper could be obtained, so no model could be trained or evaluated.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use device settings and body location to predict whether an implanted sensor receives a signal through tissue.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need one row per transmit/receive pair: pulse voltage, pulse duration, electrode spacing, which body compartment (skin, under-skin, abdominal cavity, gut), animal identity. Number of examples: unknown, and almost certainly in the tens to low hundreds.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the receiving implant switches on, or the received signal strength in millivolts, measured electrically by the receiving circuit in live rats.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: A physics-based or empirical map of which settings reach which body sites would help bioelectronics groups place implants without repeating animal surgeries. But closed-form circuit models already do this reasonably, so the gain is small.
plain_idea._note: Described for completeness; the project was not pursued because no data exists.

ml_idea: Considered: predict signal reception (on/off, or received amplitude) in a body-as-conductor communication link from pulse voltage, pulse width, electrode separation and tissue compartment. Abandoned at Part A - no obtainable data, and the realistic sample size is tens of measurements, not thousands.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; no data file was retrievable so there is nothing to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query Europe PMC for open-access status and supplementary files, then search Zenodo/Dryad/Figshare on the DOI. All four came back empty in under two minutes, which killed it.

verdict_reason: Paywalled bioelectronics device paper with no deposited data anywhere (A1 fails), and even its best case is tens of in vivo measurements, not a modellable table.
